Leveraging these Green functions' properties, we analyze the asymptotic field behavior necessary for charge existence and demonstrate a canonical phase space realization of the 2+1 BMS algebra. This discussion also includes transformations in configuration space, where the algebra only closes through skew-symmetric combinations of equations of motion. The Green function formulation enables the extension of this formalism to higher dimensions and various systems.

In two-dimensional Rashba materials with gated control, bound electron pairs (BEPs) arise from the interaction between spin-orbit effects caused by electron Coulomb fields and unique characteristics of the material's band structure resulting in negative electron mass. Our model relies on a four-band framework, specifically the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model with Rashba spin-orbit interaction originating from the gate charges. The binding energy of BEPs spans a broad range as a result of varying gate voltage across the full two-particle energy gap. Despite spin-orbit interaction eliminating spin quantization, BEPs possess a magnetic moment, primarily driven by orbital electron motion that can be manipulated by gate voltage control.

Investigations into the relationship between the confinement scale $\Lambda_c$ of a gauge theory and the Hubble scale $H$ of the background quasi-de Sitter space, constrained by the Festina Lente criteria from swampland principles, were conducted using the holographic Karch-Randall setup. This setup revealed an unstable de Sitter extremum when described solely by gravity and, while it allows a perturbative gravitational dual that satisfies Festina Lente, it does not permit an arbitrarily small parameter hierarchy. The introduction of an additional scalar sector, however, enabled metastable de Sitter minima, with Festina Lente imposing restrictions on the parameters involved. Yet, in certain scenarios where Festina Lente was found to be constraining, the metastable de Sitter minimum was found to be perilously close to decay, rendering the setup inapplicable. Furthermore, an examination of the implications of the finite lifetime of these dS extrema and their connection to related swampland conjectures found no contradictions. The findings support the Karch-Randall setup as a consistent and useful tool, provide clarity on Festina Lente's impact on holographic theories, and establish a link between Festina Lente and other swampland conjectures.

In recent years, numerous domain generalization methods have shown promising results but most are based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Meanwhile, vision transformers (ViTs), which have started to surpass CNNs on standard benchmarks, have not received the same level of attention in the context of domain generalization. Given that ViTs' performance in real-world scenarios is uncertain, this paper explores ViTs to address the domain generalization issue. Similar to CNNs, ViTs experience difficulty in handling out-of-distribution data due to overfitting to source domains. Our proposed self-distillation method for ViTs overcomes this by providing intermediate transformer blocks with non-zero entropy supervisory signals, making it easier to learn the input-output mapping problem. The approach is parameter-efficient and integrates seamlessly with various ViT backbones. Our experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of self-distillation in improving performance across multiple challenging datasets and outperforming recent state-of-the-art methods. The code and pre-trained models for our method can be found on GitHub at https://github.com/maryam089/SDViT.

This paper establishes a theoretical foundation for combining Anderson acceleration with Newton's method in nonlinear systems where the Jacobian is singular at the solution. The standard Newton algorithm converges linearly in the vicinity of the solution in such cases, yet prior research has shown that Anderson acceleration can enhance convergence significantly with minimal computational overhead. We provide an in-depth analysis of the Newton-Anderson algorithm in these scenarios and develop an innovative safeguarding approach supported by theoretical insights. Our findings are substantiated through numerical examples involving the Chandrasekhar H-equation and widely recognized benchmarks.

This paper delves into cybersecurity defence strategies by merging an innovative cybersecurity simulator with algorithms for informed decision-making through optimisation techniques. Specifically, it examines the applicability of dynamic causal Bayesian optimisation (DCBO), suggesting its potential as a proactive blue agent that leverages a network simulation and a model of how malicious activity propagates within that network. We investigate the efficacy of DCBO in optimising interventions on specific host nodes to mitigate the economic consequences of malicious intrusions. Through a comprehensive simulation framework, we generate observational data for DCBO and present numerical results, paving the way for future advancements in this area.

To test the universality of muon-to-electron interactions in b to s transitions involving lepton pairs, we define a semi-inclusive Lepton Flavour Universality ratio, $R_\Sigma$. This ratio is created by combining various decay channels, allowing for the maximum sensitivity to possible short-distance Lepton Flavour Universality violations. Its theoretical interpretation remains clear in the event of a deviation from the Standard Model prediction, $R_\Sigma^{\rm SM}$, which is 1.

The purpose of this study is to examine the invariance of the topological invariant known as non-barotropic generalized cross helicity under non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) conditions. Prior research has primarily focused on ideal barotropic MHD and ideal non-barotropic MHD. The non-ideal MHD case was largely overlooked due to its mathematical intricacy. We explore the impact of dissipative processes like thermal conduction, finite electrical conductivity, and viscosity on the conservation of cross helicity, adopting an analytical approach to derive mathematical expressions for the time derivative of cross helicity. The findings reveal that the generalized cross helicity is not conserved in non-ideal MHD conditions, while identifying the processes that affect or do not affect helicity and specifying the configurations in which this topological constant remains conserved despite dissipative processes.

We investigate the fractional Burgers equation $\Delta^{\alpha/2} u + b\cdot \nabla (u|u|^{(\alpha-1)/\beta})$ in $\mathbf{R}^d$, where $d\geq 2$, with $\alpha\in(1,2)$ and $\beta>1$. A solution exists for a broad range of initial conditions that aren't contained in any $L^p(\mathbf{R}^d)$ space, $1\leq p\leq \infty$. Specifically, for the initial condition $u_0(x)=M|x|^{-\beta}$, $1<\beta<d$, we establish the existence of a self-similar solution and explore its properties, including smoothness, bounds, asymptotic behavior, and gradient estimates.

Our study is the first to examine a sample of $eROSITA$ clusters from the $eROSITA$ Final Equatorial Depth Survey (eFEDS). By combining X-ray and optical data, we selected $455$ clusters within a specific redshift range, with $177$ systems covered by data from the Hyper Suprime-Cam survey. Using minimal assumptions, we modeled the relationships between cluster mass and observable properties, including X-ray count rates and optical richness, at each cluster's redshift. We directly measured the X-ray completeness of the clusters based on their richness distributions, which we used as informative priors for our model parameters. We validated our analysis framework using mock data and a blinded analysis of real data with consistency tests. After verifying the accuracy of our model, we obtained cosmological constraints on the matter density, $\sigma_{8}$ and the S$_{8}$ parameter, as well as the equation of state parameter of dark energy in a flat $w$CDM cosmology. Our results from the eFEDS survey align with findings from the $Planck$ mission and other studies, including those of the Dark Energy Survey and SPT-SZ survey.

Through high-resolution simulations, the statistical characteristics of the energy transfer rate to smaller scales were investigated in three distinct isotropic turbulent magnetohydrodynamic flows with varying magnetic field strengths and structures. We studied both kinetic and magnetic energy cascades, separately evaluating the distinct energy transfer contributions to overall dynamics. Our findings reveal that the local energy transfer rate distribution exhibits heavy tails, mirroring the behavior seen in hydrodynamic systems. Moreover, the individual components of the energy transfer rate exhibit distinct characteristics, and are sensitive to the type of flow analyzed. Additionally, the joint probability distribution between the local energy transfer rate and the field gradients was examined, revealing a strong correlation with magnetic field gradients, albeit with a much higher dispersion than observed in hydrodynamic flows. Furthermore, it was observed that the local energy transfer rate is influenced by the local magnetic field amplitude. The obtained results have implications for subgrid-scale modeling, which we discuss in the present study.

Autonomous vehicles and mobile robots utilize multi-beam LiDAR sensors to collect sequences of 3D scans, resulting in partially complete frames due to the sensors' limited scanning capabilities and the presence of occlusions. Although each frame is relatively sparse, the sequential collection of frames from different viewpoints compensates for these limitations and produces a more comprehensive representation of the environment. However, scenes with moving objects pose a challenge to aligning points correctly in a shared coordinate frame. This paper investigates the use of multi-frame point cloud accumulation as an intermediate step in processing 3D scan sequences and proposes a method that leverages the inherent properties of outdoor environments, including their geometric layout and the rigid nature of objects. Compared to the current state-of-the-art scene flow estimators, the presented approach more accurately aligns all 3D points in a shared frame, effectively accounting for points associated with moving objects. Consequently, this approach significantly reduces alignment errors on several benchmark datasets and enhances the quality of high-level tasks such as surface reconstruction.

The BAT AGN Spectroscopic Survey (BASS) has the ambitious goal of mapping the properties of local active galactic nuclei, including their energy output, black hole masses, feeding rates, and the obscuration caused by gas between Earth and the galaxies, as well as the characteristics of their host galaxies. This endeavor is made possible through the BASS data release 2 (DR2), the most extensive and sensitive spectroscopic survey in terms of wavelength range, resolution, and detection capabilities. The data release consists of 1449 optical spectra and 233 near-infrared spectra collected for the brightest ultra-hard X-ray-selected active galaxies across the entire sky and various levels of gas obscuration. This data provides comprehensive sets of measurements, including emission line and central velocity dispersion, with near-perfect redshift and 98% black hole mass estimates for unbeamed AGN outside the Galactic plane. The resulting sample of nearby, powerful active galaxies spans an unprecedented range of energy output, black hole masses, feeding rates, and obscuration, offering a wealth of information for understanding black hole growth, galaxy evolution, and feedback within the local universe.

The primary objective of the JWST is to investigate the initial galaxies in the universe. Our study involves a thorough examination of the most distant galaxies in the first JWST deep field near the massive cluster SMACS0723. Consequently, we discovered two potential galaxies that are about 250 million years old, dating back to the period shortly after the Big Bang. Additionally, we identified two possible galaxies at 12 billion light years away and six at 9-11 billion light years away. We extended our research to 21 billion light years by combining information from seven near-infrared filters. To verify the reliability of our photometric redshift estimates, we used two different models to analyze the Spectral Energy Distributions (SEDs). Our high-redshift galaxy discoveries typically exhibit small sizes, and their shapes are similar to those of disk-shaped galaxies. Moreover, these galaxies have very blue UV spectra and are relatively young, aged between 10 and 100 million years. Their stellar masses suggest rapid star formation and the formation of massive stars. Our findings demonstrate the capabilities of JWST to detect galaxies at extremely high redshifts, offering insights into the early formation of the universe's first galaxies.

Wormhole solutions can be determined by solving the Einstein field equations with an exemption to the null energy condition. We approach wormhole representations in κ(R,T) gravity from two angles. Firstly, we derive the shape function through the use of a redshift function and a linear equation of state, resulting in a feasible solution for realistic matter. Secondly, we examine four distinct pairings of redshift and shape functions to evaluate their respective solutions, finding that certain models may accommodate wormholes using only minimal amounts of exotic matter.

Non-Hermitian lattice Hamiltonians exhibit a distinctive energy gap and extreme sensitivity to boundary conditions, resulting from the NH skin effect which obliterates the conventional bulk-boundary correspondence. To restore this relationship for the most fundamental class of NH Hamiltonians without symmetries, we derived such Hamiltonians from the mean-field evolution of driven-dissipative cavity arrays. This approach eliminates the arbitrariness in defining the topological invariant, allowing us to treat spectra differing by a complex shift as distinct. Consequently, we found that non-trivial topological Hamiltonians form a strict subset of those with a point gap, and the NH skin effect is not of topological origin. We further analyzed the NH Hamiltonians via singular value decomposition, showing that the NH bulk-boundary correspondence is governed by an integer topological invariant, where its sign determines the localization of singular vectors at the system edge under open boundary conditions. Our work solves a long-standing problem in the theory of NH topological phases and unlocks new possibilities in topological photonics.

Our research on the iron-based superconductor FeSe$_{1-x}$Te$_x$ reveals that magnetic impurities give rise to stable zero-energy states near their locations. These impurities cause the superconductor to prefer a pairing of electrons with a specific spin alignment, as opposed to the pairing seen in the bulk material. This spin-triplet pairing preserves key symmetries and is characterized by zero modes that are topologically protected and insensitive to the direction of magnetic polarization or the distance between impurities. Theoretical predictions of this phenomenon align with experimental observations of FeSe$_{1-x}$Te$_x$.

We present the BAT AGN Spectroscopic Survey's (BASS) Near-infrared Data Release
2 (DR2), a comprehensive study of 168 local ($\bar z$ = 0.04, $z$ < 0.6) active
galactic nuclei (AGN) observed by Very Large Telescope (VLT)/X-shooter in the
near-infrared spectrum (0.8 - 2.4 $\mu$m). In our research, we observed a high
incidence of at least one near-infrared high-ionization coronal line in 45% of
Seyfert 2 and 60% of Seyfert 1 galaxies, respectively. We found that the
correlation between the emission of [Si vi] $\lambda$1.9640 and X-ray emission
is significantly tighter and less scattered compared to that of the optical [O
iii] $\lambda$5007 line. No correlation was found between the coronal line
emission and the X-ray photon index $\Gamma$. Additionally, our data revealed a
clear trend of line blueshifts with increasing ionization potential across
multiple lines. We identified a significant underestimation bias in black hole
mass measurements using broad H$\alpha$ due to dust obscuration in Sy 1.9
galaxies. Conversely, the broad Pa$\alpha$ and Pa$\beta$ lines conformed to the
$M$-$\sigma$ relation. With the combined DR1 and DR2 sample, the near-infrared
BASS sample now consists of 266 AGN, the largest NIR spectroscopic observation
dataset compiled to date.

Our research delves into the characteristics of faint radio sources found in the COSMOS field's MeerKAT International GHz Tiered Extragalactic Exploration (MIGHTEE) Early Science data, focusing specifically on the properties of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGN). Utilizing the extensive multi-spectral data in the area, we were able to categorize 88% of the 5,223 radio sources in the COSMOS field as AGN or star-forming galaxies. We identified a subset of radio-loud AGN at redshifts up to z ~ 6, characterized by radio luminosities between 10^20 and 10^27 W Hz^-1, and distinguished them as high-excitation and low-excitation radio galaxies (HERGs and LERGs). Our findings are encapsulated in a classification catalog released in conjunction with this study. Notably, we discovered that the host galaxies of HERGs and LERGs share similar properties, in contrast to previous research. Moreover, we found that the accretion rates of HERGs and LERGs are nearly identical, with the presence of a population of extremely slow accreting AGN, classified as HERGs due to their low radio luminosities. This has led us to speculate that distinguishing between HERGs and LERGs may become unnecessary at these low luminosity levels. Additionally, our research suggests that black hole mass plays a pivotal role in jet power, with a minimum mass of approximately 10^7.8 solar masses required to generate a mechanical power exceeding the radiative luminosity of the AGN (Lmech/Lbol > 1). Furthermore, we propose that a combination of high black hole mass and spin may be necessary for launching and sustaining a dominant radio jet.

The cumulative entropies of identified objects in the universe are significantly lower than the theoretical holographic maximum. Given that the entropies should be at this maximum, we propose the presence of unseen matter, specifically extremely massive, ancient black holes beyond what is found within galaxies and galaxy clusters.

Cardiovascular diseases pose a significant risk to global health, with a rising number of cases. Prompt and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment and prevention. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is a primary diagnostic tool for detecting various heart and blood vessel disorders. Conventionally, the standard 12-lead ECG is employed in clinical settings; however, employing fewer leads can facilitate ECG adoption by portable or wearable devices. This study introduces an innovative deep learning-based approach that enables the identification of multiple cardiovascular issues using only three ECG leads.

A novel interpolation method is developed to compute magnetic fields from sparse and irregularly distributed data. This method reconstructs the overall magnetic field by combining orthogonal functions and optimizes their coefficients by minimizing the discrepancy between the original and predicted magnetic fields. The constraint of zero divergence is incorporated into the cost function, enabling the approach to achieve nearly zero divergence errors. Empirical analysis reveals an exponential decay of the approximation error, outperforming local spline methods which only exhibit algebraic decay. Furthermore, the proposed method reduces computational complexity compared to computationally intensive search algorithms, while maintaining a small divergence error even in complex scenarios such as magnetic islands and stochasticity. The approach is successfully applied to calculating Poincaré sections using magnetohydrodynamic simulations and compared favorably to existing local methods.

We introduce a novel deconvolution method that accurately recovers noiseless expectation values from noisy quantum channel measurements involving multiple qubits. This protocol is universally applicable across various noise models and qubit configurations, including correlated systems. Specifically, for observables distorted by Pauli noise, our technique offers a significant quadratic speedup and ensures that the resulting noise- corrected expectation values retain their Pauli basis components. Crucially, our method enables deconvolution in scenarios where noise parameters are unknown, thereby obviating the need for resource-intensive process tomography. The effectiveness of our approach is further exemplified through theoretical case studies and simulations.

Semantic and behavioral connections hold significant importance in the development of intelligent self-driving vehicles and advanced driver assistance systems. Unlike studies focused on trajectories, locations, and object bounding, relationship information offers a comprehensible description of an object's behavior and can convey its past and future state succinctly. As a result, this data serves as a fundamental tool for identifying risks, understanding the environment, and making decisions. In this research, we propose a novel architecture, RSG-Net, which leverages a graph convolutional network to forecast potential semantic connections between objects and their surroundings, generating a graph-based output known as the "Road Scene Graph". The experimental findings demonstrate that RSG-Net, when trained on the Road Scene Graph dataset, can accurately predict semantic relationships between objects near the ego-vehicle.

In this research, we extend the scope of Proth's theorem to numbers in the form of $Kp^n+1$, resulting in a primality test that necessitates a single modular exponentiation, similar to Fermat's test but without GCD calculations. Additionally, we introduce two tests to heighten the likelihood of confirming the primality of $Kp^n+1$ numbers. As a natural outcome of these tests, we identify three families of integers $N$, whose primality can be confirmed through the verification of $a^{N-1} \equiv 1 \pmod N$ (Fermat's test). We also generalize Safe Primes, defining $a$-SafePrimes, and discuss the distribution of these numbers, proposing a conjecture regarding the related $a$-SophieGermainPrimes, which holds true for primes of 100, 1000, or 10000 digits.
All non-diagonal elements of the Moore-Penrose inverse of a tree's distance Laplacian matrix are non-positive.

We theoretically confirm that it is feasible to generate correlated entangled photon pairs with no threshold in a bimodal cavity setup consisting of a single three-level atom, stimulated by two uncoordinated sources and controlled by two coordinated fields. The entanglement of these photon pairs is shown to be possible at low intensities of the uncoordinated sources and can be solely attributed to the presence of coordinated drives. Our research indicates that dual uncoordinated stimulation with no coordinated drive leads to the amplification of cavity fields with significant anti-correlation between modes, yet no entanglement occurs. In contrast, coordinated drives with no uncoordinated stimulation are necessary to produce entangled photon pairs, but the latter cannot be amplified beyond a specific point. Conversely, even small amounts of uncoordinated stimulation in the presence of coordinated drives can significantly amplify the generated entangled photon pairs. We analyze our findings in terms of an intricate balance between coordinated and uncoordinated processes involving dressed cavity states. Both inter- and intra-mode correlation functions exhibit temporal fluctuations within the strong-coupling cavity quantum electrodynamic regime. Our theoretical model for producing nonclassical and entangled photon pairs has the potential to contribute significantly to quantum metrology and quantum information science.

A theoretical model describing a complex system exhibits a non-standard high-temperature phase where its ground state undergoes a transition from an insulating to a superconducting state, as a result of increasing a specific interaction strength that is responsible for both phases. The insulating phase's electrical resistance decreases exponentially with temperature, reaching zero at the transition point, resulting in a broad region with a unique temperature-dependent resistance behavior. As temperature increases in the superconducting phase, the system undergoes another phase transition, entering a phase where it exhibits characteristics of both a superconductor and a metal that behaves like a gas of bosons.

The Scintillating Bubble Chamber Collaboration is currently developing innovative liquid-noble bubble chambers for effectively detecting low-mass dark matter particles and coherent scattering of low-energy neutrinos without background interference. A first-of-its-kind prototype, known as SBC-LAr10, is being put into operation at Fermilab, which will test the ability of superheated argon to differentiate between background noise and low-energy nuclear recoils as low as 100 eV. In parallel, a second, highly sensitive detector is being constructed with an emphasis on minimizing radioactive contamination for the Collaboration's initial dark matter search at SNOLAB. The anticipated spin-independent sensitivity of this search is roughly $10^{-43}$ cm$^2$ at a 1 GeV$/c^2$ dark matter particle mass. The adaptability and effective suppression of background noise by the liquid-noble bubble chamber make this approach an appealing option for future dark matter searches and high-statistics studies of low-energy neutrino scattering at nuclear reactors.

This research investigates methods to create confidence sequences for restricted data sequences, drawing inspiration from the betting strategy initially developed by Hendriks and expanded upon by Jun and Orabona. Building on recent findings by Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, as well as Orabona and Jun, this study revisits Cover's concept of a universal portfolio, reinterpreting the approach from a perspective that considers two primary possibilities, or "horses." The primary contribution of this research is an algorithm based on a combination of lower bounds, capable of approximating the performance of the universal portfolio with a relatively low time cost. The study also presents an enhanced version of a previously established lower bound, which may have independent value.

Multi-agent coordination problems in real-world scenarios often involve uncertainty and lack of full information. This research focuses on a subset of such problems where humans can identify actions that intentionally reveal unusual circumstances, known as self-explaining deviations (SEDs). These actions deviate from expected norms and aim to prompt other agents to recognize the extraordinary nature of the situation through theory of mind. A real-world example and formal definition of SEDs are provided. To perform SEDs, a new algorithm called improvement maximizing self-explaining deviations (IMPROVISED) is developed. The effectiveness of IMPROVISED is demonstrated in both a hypothetical scenario and the Hanabi benchmark, marking the first method to achieve finesse plays, which exemplify human-like reasoning abilities.

High-energy excitons have a significant role in simplifying the complex physics of solids with remarkable effectiveness. Landau's Fermi-liquid and quasiparticle theories for high-temperature superconducting materials have faced skepticism, leading to the development of an alternative electron fractionalization framework, which has been successful in describing certain phenomena. Nonetheless, the application of this framework to high-temperature superconducting materials remains uncertain. Our research demonstrates that, unexpectedly, the superconductivity in optimally doped Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$ is accompanied by unusually enhanced excitonic excitation at energies significantly higher than the superconducting gap energy. This discovery provides evidence for the involvement of high-energy excitons in the superconductivity process. Consequently, the increased spectral weight of excitons imposes significant constraints on theories explaining the pseudogap and superconducting mechanisms in these materials. A two-component fermion model incorporating electron fractionalization in the pseudogap state effectively explains the observed changes, pointing to a new path for understanding the electronic structure of high-temperature superconducting materials.

In this paper, we develop a broad category of intricate non-radial, self-similar solutions for the generalized surface quasi-geostrophic equation, representing a groundbreaking construction in the field of these equations. For the first time, we provide a rigorous framework for generating self-similar solutions, with solutions exhibiting spiral patterns that are locally integrable and potentially display mixed signs. Our solutions also share some characteristics with the numerically-suggested finite-time singularity scenario proposed by Scott and Dritschel for the SQG patch setting.

The Little Glaisher theorem, which applies to all positive integers k, l, and n, asserts that two specific types of partitions of n have equal quantities: the first, consisting of parts not divisible by k and occurring less than l times, and the second, comprising parts not divisible by l and occurring less than k times. This theorem has been refined from the original Glaisher theorem through the computation of generating functions. However, despite being computationally established, the underlying reason for the equivalence of these two partition types remains unclear. Our research addresses this gap by adopting an arithmetic approach. Furthermore, we explore the feasibility of creating a Schur-type companion to the Little Glaisher theorem in the context of weighted words, specifically when l equals 2.

Four previously unknown fast radio bursts were found in the Parkes 70-cm pulsar survey data using specialized algorithms for dispersed pulses. The newly discovered FRBs exhibit exceptionally broad pulses, exceeding 50 milliseconds, and their widths are not primarily influenced by astrophysical effects. Among these, one FRB has the highest measured dispersion measure, surpassing previous records. Notably, our findings indicate that pulsar surveys remain a valuable resource for detecting unrecorded FRBs and that expanding the search duration beyond 100 milliseconds may unveil a broader class of wide-pulse FRBs.

This study introduces a pioneering control algorithm, grounded in model predictive control (MPC), for guiding a launch vehicle upper stage to optimal outcomes. The devised strategy simultaneously maximizes the vehicle's performance, robustness against external disruptions, and compliance with the splash-down constraint. Given the unpredictability of engine performance and the associated uncertainty in burn time, the suggested guidance approach incorporates a neutral axis maneuver to mitigate the sensitivity of potential impact locations to engine variability. Contrary to conventional methods for designing neutral axis maneuvers, which are often time-consuming and labor-intensive, the presented MPC algorithm automatically determines the neutral axis direction by iteratively solving a sequence of optimal control problems, thus facilitating rapid convergence to the optimal solution and permitting high MPC update rates. The efficacy and robustness of the proposed algorithm are thoroughly evaluated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations.

Researchers investigated the effects of anterior temporal lobe resection surgery on patients with treatment-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy.  This involved analyzing brain scans from 101 individuals who had undergone the surgery and comparing them to scans from the same individuals before the surgery and from a group of healthy controls. The analysis focused on how the surgery affected the shape and size of different areas of the brain both near and far from where the surgery was performed.  Results showed that the surgery led to significant changes in brain structure, particularly in regions of the brain that are connected to the part of the brain that was removed. These changes are likely due to a combination of mechanical, degenerative, and adaptive processes.

Research has found that superconducting cosmic strings can experience pinching instabilities under certain conditions. Based on this discovery, new predictions were made for when these instabilities occur, using a simplified model known as the thin string approximation. An updated analysis was developed to accurately predict the instabilities for small-scale disturbances, as the original model was not effective in these cases. Simulation studies of cosmic string perturbations confirmed the accuracy of these new predictions, demonstrating a more precise understanding of cosmic string behavior than previously known. Interestingly, the research suggests that magnetic strings may be more prone to these instabilities than expected, with instances of electric strings also exhibiting pinching instabilities. Nonetheless, studies indicate that strings approaching the chiral limit and sufficiently large vortons are generally immune to pinching instabilities.

A standard imaging process necessitates three fundamental elements: a light source that emits light, which then interacts with and scatters off the subject of interest, a detection system, and a spatially resolving detector. However, these essential components in conventional imaging scenarios are often limiting in their applicability to biological or sensitive specimens due to the lack of adequate detection capabilities and potential damage from interaction. In response, we introduce and successfully implement a quantum imaging approach that eliminates all three prerequisites. By integrating a single-photon Michelson interferometer into a nonlinear interferometer based on induced coherence and utilizing a single-pixel imaging technique, we successfully demonstrate the capability for interaction-free quantum imaging of a structured object using undetected photons. As a result, we advance the potential of quantum imaging by removing the need for object-photon interaction and significantly reducing detection requirements. This innovation opens up new possibilities for characterizing fragile samples using single-pixel imaging at silicon-detectable wavelengths.
This paper investigates the subdifferential set of an operator, examining potential connections between this set and the operator's value at points where it achieves its maximum norm.

This tribute article starts with heartfelt recollections of our dear Professor A.P. Balachandran. The main content explores our latest development of quantum mechanics within a noncommutative one-dimensional space-time structure using Hilbert-Schmidt operators. Additionally, as a practical example, we show how a geometrical phase can be observed in a forced harmonic oscillator that varies over time, set within the context of Moyal space-time.

To tackle the increasing demands for massive data communication, bandwidth efficiency, and fast data processing in Metaverse, two groundbreaking solutions have emerged: Semantic Communication (SemCom) and edge computing. Although edge computing offers accessible resources, its availability is often dependent on computing service providers, which necessitates the creation of motivating incentives for resource distribution. A recent proposal to achieve this involves the use of Deep Learning (DL)-based auctions as an incentive mechanism that maximizes revenue and adheres to essential economic principles. Consequently, this work introduces a novel design of DL-based auctions for computing resource allocation in Metaverse enabled by SemCom. Initially, the fundamentals and obstacles of Metaverse will be outlined. Next, the fundamentals and challenges of SemCom and edge computing will be discussed. Subsequently, various incentive mechanisms for trading edge computing resources will be reviewed. Afterward, the design of DL-based auctions for resource allocation in Metaverse enabled by SemCom will be presented. The outcome of simulations indicates that DL-based auctions enhance revenue while almost entirely fulfilling constraints of individual rationality and incentive compatibility.

The accuracy of competing theories or models is measured by comparing their predictive outcomes with real-world data. Consequently, the way we assess similarity directly impacts our understanding. In machine learning and scientific modeling, objective functions are often used in the form of similarity metrics, exemplified by mean squared error, which is most suitable when errors follow a normal distribution. But when this isn't the case, scientists have to determine the right measure of similarity. We investigate how information theory can assist with this choice and apply our approach to a simple hydrologic model.

The bulk photovoltaic effect, capable of generating high photovoltages, has been found to produce relatively low photocurrents. However, our study demonstrates that by manipulating the fundamental ferroelectric properties of thin BaTiO$_3$ films using epitaxial growth on various substrates, exceptionally high photoresponses can be achieved. We observed that responsivity varies non-uniformly with ferroelectric polarization and discovered a record-breaking BPE coefficient of approximately 10$^{-2}$ 1/V for planar BTO films. The standard theories explaining the bulk photovoltaic effect in bulk materials fail to account for the observed photocurrent trends, prompting the proposal of a new mechanism explaining the relationship between polarization and responsivity in ferroelectric thin films. This research indicates that the effectiveness of ferroelectric photovoltaics in standard planar geometries can be improved through a comprehensive optimization of material structure, light absorption, and electrode interface properties.

Fake news detection has evolved into a pressing concern with far-reaching societal implications, necessitating research that goes beyond mere theoretical understanding. Building upon recent breakthroughs in text-based methods, it has become evident that effectively detecting misinformation requires incorporating supplementary, context-dependent information such as how news spreads and social media user behaviors. To address this, we suggest constructing diverse, interconnected social context graphs around news articles and reframing the challenge as a graph classification task. Investigating the integration of multiple types of data and employing various graph neural network architectures suggests that this approach yields highly effective and robust outcomes on standard benchmark datasets.

Textual stance detection can be seen as an extension of textual entailment tasks in natural language processing. By viewing SD as TER, we can take advantage of increased training resources and a more versatile learning framework. This paper conducts an initial investigation into this approach, focusing on a challenging case with no existing labelled datasets, where modelling SD as TER may be most beneficial. Additionally, we incorporate knowledge from social sciences to enhance model accuracy and explore potential avenues for future research.

The widespread adoption of home-based solar energy systems has led to a recurring issue with overvoltage, primarily caused by energy flowing back into the grid in sync. Currently, photovoltaic inverters protect electronic components by limiting energy output in response to overvoltage, but this practice disproportionately affects households at the end of the power line, resulting in unequal distribution of the value of generated energy. Achieving fair distribution of this energy value through global optimization requires precise parameters of the power lines, which are often unknown. This research examines the potential of reinforcement learning, a method that gradually develops a fair strategy for curtailing solar energy production by interacting with the system. We assess six metrics of fairness to determine how effectively they can be learned compared to a hypothetical optimal solution, and our results indicate that all definitions enable efficient learning, suggesting that reinforcement learning can effectively balance fairness and safety in solar energy coordination.

Relativistic hydrodynamics has been highly effective in describing the behavior of highly interactive matter created in heavy-ion collision experiments. Recent advancements have significantly enhanced the field's ability to explain the spin polarization of hadrons produced in these processes. Although current models have accurately predicted some experimental data based on spin-vorticity coupling, there is still a lack of clarity regarding differential measurements, indicating that spin dynamics may require a more independent treatment. It is hypothesized that if the spin is a macroscopic system property, its dynamics in equilibrium should adhere to hydrodynamic principles. This thesis develops a relativistic perfect-fluid hydrodynamics framework that incorporates spin degrees of freedom derived from kinetic theory and applies it to model the dynamics of matter in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Building on experimental observations that polarization effects are minimal, we establish conservation laws for net-baryon current, energy-momentum tensor, and spin tensor based on the de Groot-van Leeuwen-van Weert pseudogauge. We further examine properties of the spin polarization tensor, its components, and analyze the propagation properties of the spin polarization components, deriving the spin-wave velocity for arbitrary statistics. Our results show that only transverse spin components propagate, similar to electromagnetic waves. The spacetime evolution of spin polarization for systems respecting certain spacetime symmetries is then studied, and the mean spin polarization per particle is calculated, enabling a comparison to experimental data. Our spin polarization results are found to qualitatively agree with certain experimental findings and other model calculations for specific observables.

A new technology, cell-free massive MIMO, is being developed to improve wireless communication systems, providing consistent coverage and high spectral efficiency compared to traditional cellular systems. This research investigates how cell-free massive MIMO can facilitate federated edge learning by utilizing the wireless channel's additive nature to enable simultaneous updates over shared communication resources. This approach, known as over-the-air federated learning, reduces the communication burden of federated learning on wireless networks. Given the complexity of the wireless channel and the limitations of available channel information, we present a feasible implementation of over-the-air federated learning using cell-free massive MIMO and analyze its convergence through both theoretical and experimental methods, highlighting the benefits of this technology.

The generation of isolated attosecond pulses (IAPs) has been significantly advanced through the application of gating techniques to limit high harmonic generation (HHG) within a single optical cycle of the driving laser. Nevertheless, this method has inherent limitations as it cannot fully utilize longer driving pulses, thus severely hindering IAP energy enhancement. In this study, we introduce a novel approach called pumping ionizing gating (PIG) to overcome these constraints. By substituting traditional ionization gating with a long pump pulse dynamically reflected off a fast-extending plasma grating, PIG enables the continuous injection of energy into the driving pulse, facilitating a more efficient transfer of energy from the pump to IAPs. We verify the efficacy of PIG through extensive particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations at a wide range of plasma densities (0.02-0.5 times critical density) and FEPG modulation depths (10-60%). The simulations demonstrate the successful generation of 330 attosecond laser pulses from 1.6-ps, 1-μm pump pulses with peak intensities 33 times that of the pump and a conversion efficiency of approximately 0.1%.

Recent research suggests that iterative least-squares MRI reconstructions should utilise the LSMR algorithm, which offers improved numerical performance compared to traditional methods like Conjugate Gradient, particularly when Toeplitz embedding is not an option for acceleration.

Recent interactions between non-Hermitian and topological concepts have given rise to an abundance of innovative research in this area, yielding numerous discoveries of novel non-Hermitian topological phenomena. This review outlines the core principles underlying the topological properties of non-Hermitian phases, with the aid of exemplary models such as the Hatano-Helson, non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger, and non-Hermitian Chern insulator, highlighting the distinctive characteristics of non-Hermitian topological systems including exceptional points, complex energy gaps, and non-Hermitian symmetry classification. The non-Hermitian skin effect and the generalized Brillouin zone concept, enabling the recovery of the bulk-boundary correspondence, are also discussed, as well as the role of disorder and linear response framework in these systems. Furthermore, concrete examples are examined to investigate the Hall transport properties of non-Hermitian topological systems and to review the rapid experimental advancements in this field, while suggesting promising future directions for exploration.

For a closed subspace within the given range space, certain conditions allow the subspace of compact operators valued in that subspace to be proximinal within the entire space of compact operators mapping to the range space.

This paper provides three separate, independently-derived proofs by the paper's three authors that prove the equivalence between the existence of a positive Birkhoff section for a given Anosov flow on an oriented three-dimensional manifold, and the condition that the flow is $\mathbb{R}$-covered and positively twisted.

One of the widely used enterprise information systems, SAP ERP, supports numerous organizational processes, including O2C and P2P. Nevertheless, the sheer volume of processes and associated data within SAP ERP makes it difficult to pinpoint specific processes and their corresponding database tables. Furthermore, isolating relevant event logs for process analysis purposes poses a considerable challenge. The presented demonstration showcases Interactive SAP Explorer, an innovative tool that addresses this challenge by representing SAP ERP's complex relational structure as a labeled property graph. This approach enables the execution of sophisticated queries and the creation of detailed representations of the system's relationships.

The spread of hateful online content poses a threat to both social media platforms and the broader society. Given the ever-changing nature of internet memes, it can be difficult to detect them. Memes that contain hateful undertones can be created by combining hateful ideas with other cultural references or symbols. This paper proposes a framework based on OpenAI's multimodal learning model CLIP to identify targets of hateful content and track the evolution of these memes over time. We discovered that CLIP can generate embeddings that highlight relationships between different types of media, such as images and text. By leveraging this capability, our framework examines how hateful memes are formed by combining different visual elements or fusing text with images. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework by analyzing antisemitic memes, including the Happy Merchant meme, and its various forms. By applying our framework to a dataset from 4chan, we found 3,300 distinct variants of the Happy Merchant meme, which are sometimes linked to specific countries, individuals, or organizations. We believe that our framework can be used to assist human moderators in identifying new forms of hateful content and help mitigate the problem of hateful online content.

Our study investigated how adding small amounts of a solute to a water-like solvent affects the temperature at which the solvent reaches its maximum density. We used a model potential with two length scales that replicates the anomalous properties of water, and introduced a solute that can interact with the solvent in various ways by adjusting the strength of its attractive forces. We observed that a highly attracted solute causes the solvent's maximum density temperature to rise, behaving like a structure former, whereas a less attracted solute causes the temperature to decrease, behaving like a structure destroyer.

Recent patch-based models such as Vision Transformers and Mixers have achieved notable success in various visual recognition tasks, surpassing classic convolutional networks. While initial patch-based models treated all patches equally, subsequent studies have shown that incorporating spatial bias enhances performance. Nonetheless, existing research primarily focused on the spatial locations of patches, neglecting the overall structure of scenes. To address this, we aim to integrate object information into the interaction of patches, introducing OAMixer (object-aware mixing layer), which adjusts patch mixing layers based on object labels. By leveraging object labels, we can derive object labels through unsupervised or weakly-supervised methods, eliminating the need for additional human annotation. Using these object labels, OAMixer generates a learnable reweighting mask that increases the interaction between patches containing similar objects. We then demonstrate that OAMixer improves the classification accuracy and robustness to background clutter for various patch-based models, including Vision Transformers, MLP-Mixers, and ConvMixers. Furthermore, OAMixer enhances the performance of downstream tasks such as large-scale classification, self-supervised learning, and multi-object recognition, confirming its universal applicability.
In this discussion, we will be examining the challenge of generating a developable surface patch with specific boundaries formed by two rational or NURBS curves.

To determine the number of minimal surfaces with a common boundary from the boundary's geometric perspective, we propose a numerical method that balances efficiency and precision. This method, grounded in the fundamental solutions approach, is supported by a thorough convergence analysis for Dirichlet energy and a precise $L^\infty$-error examination for mean curvature. Crucially, our approach produces smooth surfaces, which stands in contrast to earlier studies that necessitated the subdivision of a mesh.

The Maker-Breaker game played on a graph G involves Dominator attempting to select a dominating set and Staller trying to claim a closed neighborhood of some vertex. We explore scenarios where Staller can win this game. When Dominator starts, the minimum number of moves needed for Staller to win is represented by γSMB(G), whereas when Staller begins, it's γSMB'(G). Trees T with a minimum number of γSMB'(T) moves needed for Staller to win are characterized for every positive integer k. An upper bound on γSMB' is established using hypergraphs. For the subdivided star S derived from a star with n edges by subdividing its edges, γSMB'(S) is determined for most cases, except when the star has at least four subdivided edges, each with an even number. The most simplified formula is given when there are at least two odd-numbered subdivided edges, with the minimum values n1 and n2 resulting in γSMB'(S(n1,...,nℓ)) = ⌈log2(n1+n2+1)⌉. Additionally, exact formulas for γSMB and γSMB' are obtained for caterpillars.

In many natural and social systems, environmental changes significantly influence the development of social dilemmas. These changes encompass two primary factors: fluctuations on a global scale and local feedbacks dependent on strategy. Despite individual research on these aspects, the combined impact remains poorly understood. We propose a theoretical framework combining group strategic behaviors with their dynamic environments. The model incorporates a non-linear factor related to global fluctuations and eco-evolutionary game elements describing local feedbacks. Our results reveal distinct dynamics when comparing static and dynamic global environments. Specifically, cyclic evolutions of group cooperation and the environment emerge in an irregular pattern, contingent upon the relative speed of global and local environment changes in relation to strategy adjustments. This research provides valuable insights into the diverse outcomes of nonlinear interactions between changing environments and strategic adaptations.

Researchers have successfully applied the boundary element method to fractal screens with zero surface measure to analyze acoustic scattering. To achieve this, they utilized a non-traditional integration approach involving the Hausdorff measure. This novel "Hausdorff BEM" method was proven to converge for acoustic scattering problems in 2D and 3D spaces when the scatterer is a compact subset of a fractal set with Hausdorff dimension within a specific range. Furthermore, the researchers demonstrated that the method exhibits convergence rates and superconvergence for certain types of fractals, and they also proposed numerical integration routines to implement the Hausdorff BEM. Additionally, the researchers provided a fully discrete convergence analysis and estimated the discrete condition numbers of the method. Their findings were supported by numerical experiments involving scattering by Cantor sets and Cantor dusts in 2D and 3D spaces, respectively.

Deep learning models often underperform when encountering data from a distribution that differs from their training data. In crucial areas like medical imaging, detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples is key to improving model reliability. Recent research has developed promising DL-based methods for OOD detection in 2D medical images, but scaling these approaches to 3D images proves computationally unfeasible. Moreover, current 3D solutions struggle to accurately identify even synthetic OOD samples. This inadequate performance may suggest that DL models inefficiently handle large volumetric images. We propose an alternative approach using the intensity histogram from original CT or MRI scans as an embedding for OOD detection, finding this method to be sufficiently descriptive without the need for DL. Our proposed histogram-based method demonstrates nearly perfect performance on publicly available datasets and secures second place in the Medical Out-of-Distribution challenge, even without fine-tuning or leveraging task-specific knowledge. By examining the limitations, we conclude that our method effectively resolves the challenge of OOD detection at the sample level for 3D medical images in the current context.

We create, model, and test an acoustic metasurface consisting of a one-dimensional array of empty, hard-walled cavities, whose connections are modified through additional, underlying cavities. The complex internal design can be easily manufactured using 3D printing techniques. The unique properties of acoustic waves on this surface are affected by competing flow pathways created by these additional connections, resulting in variations in the dispersion spectrum within a specific frequency range. This design supports 'backwards' acoustic waves that move in the opposite direction of conventional waves and are experimentally confirmed. Such metasurfaces may offer improved capabilities for acoustic sensing.

A study is presented to determine the $C\!P$-even fraction in the $D^0$ decay to $K^+K^-\pi^+\pi^-$. Using a substantial dataset collected by the BESIII detector, charm meson decays are analyzed, with one reconstructed in a signal mode and the other in a $C\!P$ eigenstate or $D$ decay to $K_{S, L}^0\pi^+\pi^-$. By examining the relative rates of these double-tagged events, the result $F_+ = 0.730 \pm 0.037 \pm 0.021$ is obtained, marking the first model-independent measurement of $F_+$ in $D^0$ decays to $K^+K^-\pi^+\pi^-$.

We examine the PT-symmetric quantum Rabi model, a system comprising a PT-symmetric qubit interacting with a quantized light field, and find that it can be analytically solved within its relevant parameter range using the adiabatic approximation, thereby allowing for the exploration of its physical characteristics. Through a combination of analytical and numerical methods, including adiabatic approximation and diagonalization, the model's static and dynamic properties are thoroughly investigated. Notably, a cluster of exceptional points is discovered within the model's eigenspectrum and is linked to exactly solvable points present in its Hermitian counterpart, with these exceptional points exhibiting a peculiar behavior of vanishing and reviving in relation to the light-matter coupling strength. Furthermore, the time-dependent evolution of system observables under the Hamiltonian is analyzed, and the findings of this research can be easily extended to other light-matter interaction models, offering valuable insights into non-Hermitian quantum systems.

The advent of Gravitational-Wave astronomy is expected to allow for the identification of an astrophysical GW background resulting from unresolved binary black hole mergers, as well as the possibility of detecting primordial GW backgrounds. This will provide an ideal chance to accurately measure cosmological parameters, including the universe's equation of state, through the low-frequency tail of the GW spectrum generated by events such as phase transitions. However, there is a concern that astrophysical GW foregrounds could interfere with these efforts. Under certain conditions, these foregrounds can be assumed to be known in shape but uncertain in amplitude. In this scenario, a straightforward and efficient method can be used to isolate the primordial signal by subtracting the foreground components that closely match the signal's spectral characteristics. Our findings show that the sensitivity to primordial signals is generally limited to a few times the sensitivity in the absence of foregrounds, mainly at frequencies where the signal and foregrounds are most similar. These results stress the need for accurate models of the contributions from eccentric or intermediate-mass black hole binaries to the GW background to ensure the feasibility of precision cosmology with primordial GW backgrounds.

Using computer models, researchers investigate the evolution process in systems comprising active particles that move continuously. The findings from this study are compared with those from a 2D Ising model in a non-moving state. By simulating rapid changes in uniform configurations to specific points within the miscibility gaps and at critical points, researchers study the unsteady-state dynamics of the system. This includes calculating measurements related to structure and length scales. Additionally, the team examines aging behavior when the system is quenched into the miscibility gap, providing a detailed understanding of how the order-parameter correlation function changes over time. The observed structure and dynamics of the system are consistent with predictions from the Ising model, and similar results are seen in active lattice models for certain quenched conditions.

This paper outlines the 5th edition of the Predicting Video Memorability Task, part of MediaEval2022. For 2022, the task was reworked to foster a deeper level of analysis, while maintaining a similar setup to the previous year. Two datasets are again provided to promote generalization, but one dataset has been replaced due to quality issues, and another dataset is now prioritized, while also introducing a sub-task based on EEG for predicting short-term video memorability. The paper explains the core elements of the task, including its constituent parts, datasets, evaluation metrics, and requirements for participant submissions.

This research tackles two key challenges - developing metrics to evaluate the performance of trained AI models and deciphering how training data are encoded within these models using those metrics. These issues arise from the lack of transparency in AI systems used in safety-critical applications, such as AI-powered traffic sign classification in autonomous vehicles. To address these challenges, we establish the theoretical foundation for measuring AI model usage and analyze patterns in data encoding based on utilization patterns at the graph level of AI models. Utilization is conceptually defined as the diversity of unique outputs at each computation unit within an AI model. This study extracts utilization metrics from both benign and compromised AI models. In contrast to benign models, the compromised models were trained using images of traffic signs that had intentional, realistic modifications (triggers) to alter correct class labels. By analyzing the data encoding in both clean and poisoned AI models, we derive implications for trojan injection and detection.

Our research delves into how defect shape influences the buckling threshold of spherical shells subjected to external pressure. We conducted a comparative study on shells containing inward Gaussian defects versus outward Gaussian defects, focusing on the former as the commonly used shape and the latter as the lesser-explored alternative. Utilizing validated finite-element simulations, we examined the effects of defect geometry on the buckling resistance of both types, taking into account varying defect parameters. Our findings show that spherical shells with outward Gaussian defects consistently display significantly higher buckling resistance than those with inward Gaussian defects, regardless of defect amplitude and width. Furthermore, the relationship between buckling resistance and defect parameters differs between the two cases, which also exhibit distinct behavior beyond the buckling point. Our results are interpreted through the lens of the varying mean curvature of the two defect types.

Predicting a classifier's performance on new data often depends on validation sets, 
but these are scarce in few-shot learning applications, where this limitation is 
overlooked. In such cases, researchers often use pre-trained neural networks and 
nearest class mean classifiers. Our approach involves creating a Gaussian model 
for feature distribution and using its parameters to forecast a classifier's 
performance on new tasks. The key to our success lies in accurately measuring 
distances between class-specific probability distributions, which we estimate 
fairly. We demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional leave-one-out 
cross-validation methods in low-sample environments.

Recent research involving intense laser beams and atomic gases has created a complex many-body system that, when scaled up, forms a boundary time-crystal. This unique state of matter is stabilized by the balance between coherent energy and collective loss. An experiment allowing real-time observation of the system's behavior has been conducted. Our findings indicate that monitoring the light field's state can provide insight into the system's non-equilibrium dynamics. The photon count signal and homodyne current reveal distinct features of the system at its phase transition, including gradual changes and sudden spikes. Notably, the time between these spikes increases as the system size grows, following a power-law pattern, which can be attributed to a simple non-linear phase model. Additionally, the time-integrated homodyne current can be used as a reliable order parameter, signifying the coexistence of various oscillation patterns within this state of matter.

The Antarctic ice sheet's decadal mass loss drives elastic uplift rates in the ANET GNSS network, with rates of up to 20 mm/yr. For the first time, researchers investigate whether the elastic deformation recorded in the ANET GNSS network can be used to estimate ice mass changes in Antarctica. To achieve this, the regions of ice mass loss contributing to elastic deformation at each ANET GNSS site were determined using a model of elastic deformation, called a Load Sensitivity Kernel (LSK). The results indicate that the majority of ANET sites are primarily affected by mass changes occurring at distances greater than 200km. Furthermore, by analyzing the differences in LSKs between neighboring GNSS receivers, researchers can localize near-field mass changes. A novel approach was developed that utilizes multiple GNSS sites and weights their LSKs to minimize elastic deformation caused by external mass changes. This approach enabled researchers to isolate the elastic deformation resulting from the PIG glacier's and the PSK glaciers' mass losses using 7 ANET GNSS sites in the Amundsen Sea region. Additionally, it was found that the current ANET configuration can be used to estimate ice mass changes in Antarctica, particularly in regions with a high concentration of GNSS receivers.

We delve into the realm of satisfiable formulas in satisfiability modulo theories (SMT), specifically focusing on the automated creation of numerous satisfying solutions for these formulas. Although SMT has a long and successful track record in model checking and formal verification, this aspect remains relatively under-examined. Existing research has explored generating samples or assignments for Boolean formulas and quantifier-free first-order formulas involving bit-vectors, arrays, and uninterpreted functions. Our approach introduces a new method applicable to a theory of integer arithmetic, as well as integer arithmetic combined with arrays and uninterpreted functions. This method involves reducing the sampling problem to a more manageable instance of interval sampling, which can be efficiently executed. This reduction is achieved by expanding a single seed model using top-down constraint propagation through the original first-order formula.

This study presents the first measurement of the spin alignment of D*+ vector mesons and their antiparticles relative to the helicity axis, which occurs through charm-quark formation in hadron collisions or beauty-meson decay. These measurements were taken at the ALICE detector in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. By examining the D*+ decay into D0 mesons, researchers found that D*+ mesons formed through prompt processes showed no alignment, while D*+ mesons formed through non-prompt processes showed signs of alignment with a value of 0.455, consistent with a Monte Carlo simulation. The observed alignment could mimic global spin alignment in heavy-ion collisions, suggesting that further investigation is required to distinguish between these effects.

We derive general expressions for the oblique correction parameters $S$, $T$, $U$, $V$, $W$, and $X$ in a Standard Model extension featuring quark multiplets of arbitrary size with specified electric charges, which are allowed to mix with standard quarks of corresponding charges.

The NA61/SHINE experiment, located at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron, focuses on researching the critical point of strongly interacting matter and the onset of deconfinement through a comprehensive study of particle interactions. This research includes examining hadron production in various collisions such as nucleus-nucleus, proton-proton and proton-nucleus interactions, across different energy levels and nucleus sizes. In this presentation, the results of newly acquired data on the production of identified charged kaons in the collisions of intermediate-sized nuclei (argon and scandium, and beryllium and beryllium) at the specified CERN beam momentum range will be shared. Furthermore, the newly measured production of strange mesons, resonances, and baryons in proton-proton collisions will also be discussed.

As the world shifts towards decarbonization, integrating renewable energy sources into the grid is creating new hurdles and opportunities for battery energy storage systems (BESS) participating in the energy market. Energy trading and frequency control services can be lucrative for BESS due to rising price fluctuations in the spot market and the capability to respond quickly to grid stability needs. To maximize profits under uncertain market conditions, BESS must carefully allocate capacity to various markets. This paper approaches the BESS's bidding problem as a Markov decision process, enabling it to participate in both spot and frequency control markets for optimal profit. By employing the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm, the BESS can learn a bidding strategy from real-world market dynamics and continuous bidding scales. Using historical data from the Australian National Electricity Market, the proposed model demonstrates that a joint bidding strategy in both markets yields significantly higher profits than separate market participation.

The DS-NER method helps to overcome the NER data scarcity issue by automatically generating training samples. However, this may result in noisy labels which can weaken model performance and limit its practical use. To address this, researchers have started to use self-training frameworks to refine labels and improve NER model generalizability. Yet, these frameworks are often underperforming due to simple designs, such as weak student learning and teacher updates. This paper proposes an innovative solution by introducing two improvements: (1) a dynamic teacher learning system, which combines two teacher-student networks to provide a more complete student learning process, and (2) a fine-grained student ensemble technique, which updates the teacher model with a moving average to ensure consistency against noise. Through experiments on four DS-NER datasets, we confirm the effectiveness of our method by achieving superior results compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

A groundbreaking technique called spatial transcriptomics has the potential to revolutionize the study of RNA expression within tissues. Traditional methods that measure gene expression at the level of multiple cells need complex deconvolution to extract information from individual cells. The rapid progress in measuring RNA expression at the subcellular level has created a need for a new approach. We have developed a novel method called TopACT that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with high-resolution spatial data, enabling automatic identification of different cell types. Unlike existing methods, TopACT can pinpoint the location of isolated cells within complex tissue structures without prior knowledge of cell boundaries. By combining TopACT with advanced topological analysis, we have made significant discoveries about the spatial organization of immune cells within kidney tissues in a mouse model of lupus, which our experiments have confirmed. Our new method seamlessly integrates data from various biological scales, from individual genes to the overall organization of tissues.

We establish the optimal Lipschitz regularity of weak solutions for the measure-valued elliptic partial differential equation, given by $-\mathrm{div}(A(x) \nabla u) = Q \, \mathcal{H}^{n-1} \llcorner \Gamma$ within a smooth domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The hypersurface $\Gamma$ is characterized by a $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity, and the density $Q$ on $\Gamma$ is represented by a $C^{0,\alpha}$ function, whereas $A$ is a symmetric, uniformly elliptic, and $W^{1,q}$-regular matrix where $q > n$. We investigate the optimality of these conditions for the given data. This PDE can be viewed as a unique combination of two $A$-harmonic functions separated by the interface $\Gamma$, playing a pivotal role in multiple free boundary problems as demonstrated in the following discussion.

One of the key principles of quantum theory, the Born rule, calculates the probability of obtaining a specific outcome from a given quantum state by squaring the absolute value of the wavefunction's overlap with that state. This rule has proven highly successful in making accurate predictions, yet it lacks a straightforward method of direct verification. However, a proposed experiment demonstrates that it is feasible to measure the superposition wavefunction using weak values, thereby enabling a direct verification of the Born rule.

In high-dimensional complex data, matrix factorization assumes that meaningful information resides within lower-dimensional patterns, which provide valuable insights through interpretable sparse structures.  These sparse patterns are advantageous for regularization and reducing overfitting. We propose a computationally efficient Bayesian method for high-dimensional matrix factorization, modeling the relationship between rows and columns using flexible sparse patterns within factors. This approach can incorporate external information, allowing for structure identification without imposing it. Building on boosting algorithms, we develop a sequential strategy for estimating low-rank contributions, with a data-driven stopping criterion. This approach's practical benefits are illustrated through simulations and analysis of soccer heatmaps from advanced tracking data.

This study evaluates the capabilities of a prototype for the Near Detector's High Angle Time Projection Chambers, which are being integrated into the T2K experiment's upgrade. The two chambers of the Near Detector will utilize 32 advanced sensors on their endplates, enabling the precise detection of ionization electrons and their associated track positions. Our research incorporates the first sensor produced for the T2K project, along with the chamber's readout electronics, which were tested using the DESY Test Beam to assess spatial and energy resolution. The performance characteristics of these sensors are analyzed and compared to a newly developed simulation, demonstrating spatial resolution below 800 micrometers and energy resolution under 10% across all relevant angles and distances. Our simulation accurately reproduces the data and confirms that the prototype meets the necessary standards for the T2K High Angle Time Projection Chambers.

In a preceding study (arXiv:2210.16738[hep-th]), we established a set of constraints 
relating flavor masses that are necessary for the $\beta$-deformed $A_{n-1}$ quiver 
matrix model to exhibit maximal symmetry at large scales with massive states, 
and we also found evidence for an Argyres-Douglas critical hypersurface. In this 
letter, we work out the precise requirements for the model's moduli parameters 
to cause the Seiberg-Witten curve to degenerate as much as possible, while still 
satisfying the constraints on flavor masses, and these conditions define the 
Argyres-Douglas hypersurface.

Our study examines the bounce solution in holographic QCD and electroweak models featuring a first-order phase transition. Calculations based on the holographic bounce solution indicate that key parameters in the gravitational wave power spectrum are significantly different from those found in field theory. Notably, these parameters, including $\alpha$ and $\beta/H$, suggest a fast and strong phase transition. In the holographic model, the critical, nucleation, and percolation temperatures of the phase transition are relatively close. Moreover, the bubble wall velocity is found to be below the sound speed of the plasma, which is indicative of a deflagration scenario. For the QCD phase transition, the expected gravitational wave power spectrum is within the detectable range of BBO and Ultimate-DECIGO, while for the electroweak phase transition, it can be detected at frequencies between 1-10 Hz. Our results also show that the formation of primordial black holes is not favored due to the relatively large value of $\beta/H$ and low velocity $v_w$.

This research examines left-invariant Finsler metrics defined by a conic structure on a two-dimensional non-Abelian Lie group, characterized by spray vector fields that never disappear. We classify these metrics according to their curvature, Landsberg, or Berwald properties. We show that any left-invariant conic metric satisfying the Landsberg condition must also meet the Berwald condition. This finding allows us to formulate a hypothesis, the homogeneous conic Landsberg Conjecture, which posits that all homogeneous Landsberg metrics are Berwald, and we prove this for two-dimensional cases.

One of the primary obstacles in the development of neural control system technology lies in verifying the safety and resilience of neural network (NN) controllers in the face of uncertainties stemming from unaccounted dynamics, non-linearities, and time delays. To address this issue, researchers propose using a robust reference model to evaluate the closed-loop system's performance. This paper presents an innovative method to evaluate the performance and resilience of complex systems featuring NN controllers and subject to uncertainties. By transforming the problem into a tracking error analysis between a closed-loop system and a reference model, the study employs the differential mean value theorem and the integral quadratic constraints technique to approximate the controller error. Additionally, the study establishes the relative integral square error and supreme square error bounds for the output of the error dynamical system. By combining Lyapunov theory with the IQCs-based approach, the analysis yields worst-case predictions for the RISE and SSE between the reference model and the uncertain system. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through its application to a nonlinear single-link robot system, where a trained NN controller was used to simulate the movement of the system while adhering to an ideal reference model.

In quiver gauge theories and dimer models, amoebae from tropical geometry and Mahler measure from number theory demonstrate significant connections and shared dependencies on the Newton polynomial coefficients via the Ronkin function. Genetic algorithms are employed to identify the numerical relationships between the components of 2d and 3d amoebae and the Mahler measure, revealing a polynomial connection between the volume of amoeba complements and the gas phase contribution to Mahler measure in dimensions 2 and 3. Further analyses extend to non-reflexive Mahler measure and machine learning is applied to learn the 3d amoebae topology with high accuracy, accompanied by the derivation of analytic expressions for certain amoebae boundaries.

The graph partitioning problem, being a core combinatorial optimization issue, has garnered substantial attention from both theoretical experts and practitioners owing to its extensive applications. Various techniques, including multilevel graph partitioning and specialized optimization solvers like Gurobi and CPLEX, have been developed. However, understanding the constraints of these approaches is essential to overcome the computational limitations of this problem.
